headline_marked: Samsung Gallery [[secret menu]] unlocks hidden photo features
headline: Samsung Gallery secret menu unlocks hidden photo features
summary: Unlock experimental features like Private Albums and AI Zoom by accessing a hidden menu within your Samsung Gallery app.
details: Samsung users can access a hidden 'Gallery Labs' menu to unlock experimental features not yet released to the public. This menu is similar to developer options on Android, offering a glimpse into future app functionalities.

To enable Gallery Labs, open the Gallery app, navigate to Settings, then 'About Gallery.' Repeatedly tap the version number until a confirmation message appears. The Gallery Labs menu will then be accessible from the 'About Gallery' screen.

One of the most useful features found in Gallery Labs is 'Private Albums,' which allows users to securely store sensitive images. This feature, now officially part of One UI 8.5, was previously available as an experimental option.

Another notable feature is 'AI Zoom,' which enhances the clarity and sharpness of images when zooming in, particularly beneficial for older photos or low-quality screenshots. This can make text in screenshots more readable.
Gallery Labs also offers a 'Restore files in Private album' option, allowing users to recover accidentally deleted private photos. This provides an extra layer of security for sensitive content.

For users who experienced issues with private albums disappearing after the One UI 8.5 update, Gallery Labs may offer a fix through 'Private Album Recovery,' specifically addressing problems with albums saved in Samsung's Secure Folder.

headline_marked: [[Chinese court freezes $318M]] in Nexperia assets amid Wingtech dispute
headline: Chinese court freezes $318M in Nexperia assets amid Wingtech dispute
summary: A Chinese court has frozen over $318 million in assets belonging to chipmaker Nexperia, as its parent company Wingtech seeks to regain control. Nexperia states this won't impact daily operations.
details: A court in Dongguan, China, has frozen 2.14 billion yuan (approximately $318 million) in assets of Dutch chipmaker Nexperia and its equipment arm, ITEC. The order, valid until August 2029, covers Nexperia's equity in five Chinese subsidiaries and ITEC's stake in its subsidiary.

This move comes as part of Wingtech Technology's year-long legal battle to regain control of Nexperia, which Dutch authorities had previously stripped from it. Wingtech filed an $1.19 billion damages claim against Nexperia and its executives in May.

The frozen entities are the same Chinese operations that ceased following Nexperia's headquarters' instructions last October, leading to accusations of unauthorized bank accounts and refusal to pay for delivered wafers.

Nexperia stated that these measures pertain only to entities operating outside its governance and will not affect its day-to-day operations, management, or business continuity. The company has been working to qualify domestic wafer suppliers and produce chips on 12-inch wafers.

Wingtech's financial situation appears strained, with first-half revenue down over 90% year-over-year and a significant net loss. Its shares are under a delisting-risk designation after an auditor couldn't verify a substantial portion of its assets.
